title: Knowledge check: Dependency and Configuration Security

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Dependency and Configuration Security”?
options: Use a hidden frontend button as the only authorization check.
Treat a VITE_ environment variable as secret because it came from .env.
Render untrusted values as escaped text, validate input and URLs, and enforce access decisions on the backend.
Compile untrusted strings as Vue templates to make them interactive.
questions.answer_key: Render untrusted values as escaped text, validate input and URLs, and enforce access decisions on the backend.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Dependency and Configuration Security directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “Keeping dependencies updated”, which practice is most reliable?
options: Color is enough to identify every form error.
Use safe text interpolation, semantic controls, accessible names, and enforce sensitive access decisions on the backend.
Use v-html for all user-supplied strings.
A hidden frontend button enforces authorization.
questions.answer_key: Use safe text interpolation, semantic controls, accessible names, and enforce sensitive access decisions on the backend.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “Keeping dependencies updated”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Dependency and Configuration Security” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.

review_note: Answer keys and explanations are server-side data. Human review required before publication.
